items.title: Al Tinney interviewed by Monk Rowe, Buffalo, New York, October 14, 2002
items.q: They were great practicers in my day. That’s why they were all so good. Like Bird and Diz and the rest of them

ctx.x: Hell yeah. Because they weren’t eating. All their money was going into the drug situation. They were feeding the drug dealer. And actually they were living reclusively you know, by themselves, and just banging up all day or doing something, and nothing

else interested them except maybe their music, which they would maybe practice for four or five hours at a time. They were great practicers in my day. That’s why they were all so good. Like Bird and Diz and the rest of them, Charlie — what’s his name now — he was a trumpet player — Charlie Shavers, that’s his name. And they were all terrific and because of their practice. They practiced, like they say you want to get to Carnegie Hall? Practice. And they finally made it to Carnegie Hall, believe it or not — not in…
Well it must have been quite a challenge working with guys like Don Byas and so forth?
